title: TMX Environment Provider Manifest
description: Schema for an Environment Provider manifest. A provider materialises the `environment` block of a Flow into real resources. It is implemented either as a standalone binary (invoked by the core TMX CLI) or as a Flow that implements the standard methods. Every provider must implement bootstrap, deploy, clean and destroy.

kind.description: Artifact discriminator. Identifies this document as a provider manifest.

name.description: Provider name, as referenced by an environment's `provider` field.

type.description: How the provider is implemented. `binary` — a standalone executable invoked by the core TMX CLI; `flow` — a Flow whose tasks implement each method.

binary.description: Path or name of the standalone executable. Used when `type` is `binary`.

optionsSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema (inline object or a $ref/path string) describing the provider-specific `environment.options` this provider accepts. Lets the CLI validate environment definitions against the chosen provider.

methods.description: The standard lifecycle methods every provider must implement.

bootstrap.description: Bootstrap the environment to enable Flow runs (e.g. provision network, create clusters).

deploy.description: Create what is required for a specific (or set of) Flow runs.

clean.description: Remove deployed instances used for Flow runs.

destroy.description: Destroy the entire environment, including everything created by bootstrap.

method.title: Provider method implementation
method.description: How a single provider method is carried out. For `binary` providers this is typically the subcommand string the CLI invokes; for `flow` providers it is a Flow reference, an inline list of TMX tasks, or a Flow import.

oneOf.description: A subcommand (binary providers) or a Flow reference (flow providers).
Inline list of TMX tasks. Items conform to the task schema in tmx.schema.json.

use.description: Reference to a Flow implementing this method.

inputs.description: Input variables passed into the referenced Flow, keyed by the input names it declares.
